result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): A builds its plan on an inventory of actual usage, keeps a separate large shadow for the modal, and correctly warns that snapping to the new scale will cause visible changes. B gives more concrete token values and catches the fragile .btn-big modifier, but it calls the snapping 'mostly invisible', treats the modal as the same concept as card and panel, and states contrast failures that assume a white background it can't see. A also says 'four' shadows but lists only three, a small slip that doesn't outweigh B's problems. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers find the same near-duplicates and quote specific values. B separates intentional elevation from accidental drift: it keeps the modal's large shadow and asks whether the panel is needed at all. B also says plainly that snapping values to the scale will cause small visible changes, and it starts with a usage inventory instead of guessing. A calls snapping 'mostly invisible', which is wrong. A also treats card, panel and modal as one concept, and it states a contrast ratio that assumes a white background the excerpt never shows.
